summary: Persistent-staging Project Memory promotion tooling (aa219a6) gave spreadsheet-edited canonical JSON a review boundary; independent review (56f4a04) found the boundary decorative -- diff-as-gate rejected the intentional edits it was meant to admit, staging could go stale or partial before promotion, and Make prerequisite ordering could let a different staged state be promoted than the one diffed. A strong correction (d201af5) added isolated validated import, exact table-set validation, canonical-baseline and staged-proposal fingerprints, stale-baseline/stale-proposal refusal, failed-import preservation, and one-shot proposal-marker consumption, closing the first two findings and partially closing the third. Independent rereview (773ea97) confirmed those closures but reproduced 14-of-30 double-success concurrent `memory-promote` runs: the marker-load/compare/write/consume sequence is not an exclusive critical section, so two simultaneous promotions can both validate and both consume the same reviewed proposal.
notes: Concurrent-promotion finding accepted as valid and left unfixed by maintainer decision rather than remediated with locking; see DEC-WFC-010.

summary: The forward simplification named by DEC-WFC-010 was implemented. The persistent staged-proposal protocol -- tracked staging directory, approval marker, canonical-baseline and staged-proposal fingerprints, one-shot consumption, and `memory-promote` as a custom acceptance operation -- was removed and replaced by `memory-export` / `memory-import` / `memory-roundtrip-check` over two persistent representations only (canonical JSON and the editable ODS workbook), with Git as the review, acceptance, and rollback boundary. Import converts into a throwaway directory outside the repository and validates the complete expected table set before replacing canonical JSON, refuses when canonical already carries uncommitted changes, and refuses a canonical directory a symbolic link redirects outside the repository.
notes: Independently reviewed at 9b9e99e (2026-09-28): CHANGES REQUIRED with 0 BLOCKING, 0 IMPORTANT, 1 MINOR (F-M1, the false blanket `make -j` parallel-safety claim, still present at HEAD) and 1 INFO. The implementation itself was found correct for the documented serial maintainer flow. The concurrent-promotion finding from 773ea97 becomes moot rather than fixed: no promotion operation remains to race. No locking, lease, journal, or transaction machinery was added.

summary: The pragmatic Operator Harness v0 concept was recorded and then implemented through ordinary maintainer commits rather than a WFC Run -- their subjects carry no WorkItem/Hop identity token, which a trusted WFC commit must -- as repository-owned `scripts/wfc_op.py` with four deterministic subcommands -- prepare, launch, status, archive -- replacing the large hand-authored PREPARE/LAUNCH shell blocks that earlier Runs such as S4-005 had required. PREPARE pins exact Development/Runtime/Evidence HEADs, enforces clean Development/Evidence and a clean detached push-disabled Runtime, exports and installs the pinned Runtime outside all three clones, writes execution-bindings.yaml from explicit --role-binding inputs only, assembles and verifies the controlled PATH, runs the pinned Runtime's own provider-free preflight, materializes launch.sh, and stops at PREPARED / NOT LAUNCHED. `docs/wfc_operator_manual.adoc` was added as the operator-facing manual for the same surface.
notes: Harness v0 adds no semantic workflow authority; see DEC-WFC-016. The manual is current operator practice but is not yet classified in the `docs/README.adoc` authority index.

summary: The Projected Result Contracts concept was recorded and its P1 slice -- projection infrastructure -- was implemented (RUN-157080a2fa7b44de8429aa9b8fba53ab), independently assured by a fresh successor Run with verdict ACCEPT, and promoted to Runtime: one closed provider-neutral ResultContractKind; one pure select_result_contract(profile, phase, run) selector reading only declared facts and never a phase-key string; the selected kind threaded through AgentExecutionRequest; the dispatched kind/version pair persisted as a sibling pair on Hop/HopSummary, with replay requiring a complete recorded pair, failing closed on an incomplete or unsupported one, and falling back truthfully for legacy history. Every then-admitted profile still selected the pre-existing generic RoutingResult: P1 built the seam, not new semantics. The roadmap was then revised to add P3.5 and sharpen P4, independently reviewed, and closed.

The reducer behaved correctly throughout.

summary: P2 made WorkResult (status: completed|blocked) and ReviewVerdict (verdict: accept|changes_required) genuinely distinct frozen types with disjoint strict provider schemas, so a worker can no longer express a review-style disposition at all, while the generic RoutingResult v1/v2 path remains for convergence roles. It took three non-accepting Runs first. An independent stagnation audit localized the cause to Commission/profile topology -- full-suite pytest on worker phases that structurally cannot route an evidence failure, review gates without failed_evidence_route, and prompt prose making downstream acceptance evidence a worker completion prerequisite -- rather than to the implementation, the environment, or the model. Once the corrected topology was commissioned, P2 Integration Completion (RUN-26e233c979554260bcca8529d1b72c1f) finished in two Hops with trusted pytest PASS, and the first genuine broad P2 review returned ACCEPT.
notes: The audit's explicit model conclusion: this episode does not show that WFC requires frontier models for basic operation; the system made ordinary model mistakes unusually expensive because each Commission permitted effectively one Hop before a routine negative acceptance signal terminated the Run. The stopped Run's useful Slice4B change was preserved as non-authoritative salvage (405f3b2) and carried no review or correctness credit.

summary: The evidence-failure disposition design was recorded and implemented over a three-Commission lineage. Admission now refuses a profile that places Coordinator-required evidence on a non-gate phase, or on a required-evidence gate with no failed_evidence_route. Run A (RUN-c661748adf434e74bcf0e15f2b05ff9f) implemented the rule and then demonstrated it against itself: H002's semantic ACCEPT was correctly overridden by a failing Coordinator-owned full pytest which the declared failed_evidence_route moved into correction, and H003 fixed the in-scope regressions but stopped because the remaining failure was an architecture test outside its authorized scope. Run B stopped on a mechanically preempted rereview that returned semantic ACCEPT while omitting the required durable-artifact CommitIntent. Run C (RUN-65952de309aa4c4bb21a762640d64929) closed the stale Harness fixture in two Hops with trusted PASS.
notes: Run A's H003 stop is the empirical trigger for the Level-1 architecture-disposition concept: an architecture-test conflict can mean candidate defect, stale architecture test, or a real architecture decision, and an ordinary correction agent is not the right authority to collapse the three into 'make pytest green'. Useful dirty H003 work was separately salvaged (02c08ad, left in ordinary Development history, predating the dedicated-candidate-ref refinement). The accepted rule is DEC-WFC-012, and it is the rule the first version of the P3 Commission violated two days later, caught by that Commission's second provider-free PREPARE refusal.

summary: A wave of records separated Level-0 recording from Level-1 interpretation: product-boundary section 4.4 (a terminal Level-0 stop is local termination plus a higher-level control signal, with authority-bounded catch/propagate -- see DEC-WFC-015); the Level-1 architecture-disposition concept; the run-event and review-artifact concept (semantic review is not final gate acceptance, one meaningful Hop should normally leave one trusted commit, defaults should be derivable and explicit paths should be overrides); the successor/Commission pipeline target (a SuccessorIntent plus a deterministic Commission Compiler, staged by maturity); and the escalation/candidate-handoff concept with its Commission / Slice-implementation-concept / Epic / programme escalation ladder.
notes: All non-authorizing. The unifying principle recorded is 'L0 records what happened; L1 interprets what it means for the project', and the manually curated semantic Run ledger in `workflow-coordinator-run-evidence` is explicitly a temporary, hand-simulated Level-1 projection rather than a mandatory execution artifact. The candidate Level-1 duty list is deliberately broader than escalation classification plus Commission authoring. Each record restates the mechanism-admission rule: add Level-0 mechanism only for observed failure or concrete imminent need, after asking whether Commission, profile, policy, scope, review, evidence, documentation, or convention already suffice.

summary: The P3 Finding-projection design record was promoted with its one blocking design question maintainer-resolved (a same-state Finding citation is an evidence-only act and does not require finding_authority, which gates state-changing transitions only; citation and transition should therefore be structurally distinct result variants), and a four-file P3 Commission was committed at d2adf08 after two provider-free PREPARE refusals -- a persona over 512 UTF-8 bytes, and required evidence on a non-gate worker phase. Because the blocked result carried no trusted CommitIntent its useful in-scope changes stayed dirty, and the Coordinator separately fail-closed on the dirty worktree.

The stop is positive evidence for the Level-0 authority boundary rather than an implementation failure, and the remaining friction is above Level 0. The useful candidate was manually preserved as ccd1d57, which touches nine paths in total -- four source paths (codex_adapter.py, model.py, reducer.py, serialization.py) and five paths under `tests/` (tests/support.py plus four test modules), with src/workflow_coordinator/adapter.py untouched, reachable only via refs/wfc/candidates/RUN-8875175a2ea343adbaf47c105699f91e/H001, not an ancestor of `main`, and carrying no authority and no review credit. summary: An empirical friction record was preserved so a later simplification effort would start from evidence rather than recollection. Drawing on the curated Run ledger, committed design and Commission artifacts, and labelled maintainer-session observations, it documents the 2026-10-11 P3 session (a planned 30-minute 'quickly start this Run' window exceeding 45 minutes, two provider-free PREPARE refusals, a failed PREPARE consuming a human-meaningful attempt identifier, and a first real Hop that returned control immediately) plus corroborating lineages back to September. Its working hypothesis: the dominant complexity is the distributed specification and lifecycle machinery around the evaluator-optimizer loop, not the loop; a second hypothesis is that the repository increasingly relies on an AI maintainer carrying historical context that should be mechanically derivable from fewer canonical declarations. It also records baseline metrics to capture before any redesign and candidate simplification principles, of which the cheapest add no new mechanism.
notes: Non-authorizing empirical observation. It explicitly does NOT establish that WFC is over-engineered, that independent review should be removed, that fail-closed behavior is too strict, that the P3 stop is a WFC defect, that long assistant context definitively degrades models, that repository LOC proves architectural complexity, that any slice should be skipped, or that a specific simplification architecture is known. Its stated sequencing preference -- finish P3, P3.5, P4, P5 and the Claude-adapter/provider-neutrality dogfood before making simplification the primary programme -- is a dated planning observation, not authorization.

summary: The 'Commissioning Service' hypothesis -- one new layer between Level 1 and Level 0 owning task assessment, workflow-pattern selection, role/persona projection, model policy, evidence and capability profiles, data-zone projection and deterministic compilation -- was recorded (54a125c), independently reviewed (b76f76c: ACCEPT WITH MATERIAL REVISIONS, 0 BLOCKING, 5 MATERIAL), and amended to incorporate all five findings (009aed3). The conclusion is partly negative: the hypothesis straddles the existing trust boundary, because one component would both decide what authority to request and whether that request is admissible, and must be split. The surviving direction places project semantics, semantic authoring, deterministic provider-free Commission projection and request-side preferences above the boundary, with authority originating in a separately protected source, and keeps admission, trusted enforcement, mandatory capability/information-flow/assurance derivation where such mechanisms exist or are later built, trusted evidence, governed effects and fail-closed execution inside Level 0. No new monolithic trust-bearing service between the levels is accepted as needed; Commission compilation is better understood as an authority-free requesting-side projection.
notes: NON-AUTHORIZING throughout. A review verdict of ACCEPT WITH MATERIAL REVISIONS is not implementation authority, and the amended record is at most the preferred current architecture hypothesis; it authorizes no CommissionIntent/Compiler/TaskAssessment schema, no catalog, no grammar, and no source, test, scripts, or governance change. Amendments of record: CommissionIntent would be a canonical AUTHORING source for one render transaction while the committed and admitted governing inputs remain the canonical EXECUTION authority, and current Level 0 knows no CommissionIntent; current authority is a separately trusted maintainer/operator reviewing or approving the exact bundle, Git recording, transporting, pinning and auditing it, and a separate maintainer act authorizing PREPARE/LAUNCH against the pinned state, so repository state alone is not proof of authorization and 'commit = authority' is wrong; a standing TaskAssessment fixture relocates rather than resolves the recursion and stays open design; the amended concept now allows that trusted policy could eventually impose a minimum model capability/assurance floor where a control genuinely depends on competence, with no router, score, provider-policy schema, or model taxonomy implied; and the corrected corpus is 36 profiles, 124 phases, 12 phase-name sets and five raw WORK/GATE signatures reducing to one repeating WORK/GATE unit occurring once or twice plus legitimate gate-first continuation entry offsets, with one uncovered bypass edge in `standalone-developer-ergonomics` -- so no workflow grammar is accepted until lossless or semantically equivalent round-trip coverage of the full corpus is demonstrated. The proposed six-variant escalation ontology was rejected as net-negative: the implemented closed set remains scope, semantic_authority, public_surface, trust_boundary, prerequisite, operational, and architecture disposition is an orthogonal classification rather than a new kind.

summary: The simple workflow capability (a genuinely single-agent-invocation programme: one bounded Worker assignment, self-check within the same invocation, no mandatory second agent invocation, no independent semantic reviewer, no correction/review loop) was named a Level-0 MVP requirement (2026-10-31 maintainer decision) and delivered the same day. The accepted Level-0 architecture design (Run RUN-fd99befee6734b7aba04f94773013ddd, Findings F002/F004) named two source-level prerequisite defects, BUG-WFC-PROVIDER-TRANSPORT-CANDIDATE-ACCEPTANCE and BUG-WFC-COMMISSION-SELECTED-COMPONENT-PROVENANCE; both were resolved by the implementation WorkItem (WI-WFC-SIMPLE-V1-IMPLEMENTATION-001, Run RUN-db5e75585299482d94af21df22b36eb4), final accepted Development HEAD dd0eab2ee1ae6ed21d266438c0aa6812e8824c4f. notes: Does not claim PyPI Beta, Claude integration, token accounting, or full operator release hardening is complete. The implemented runtime lets the sole Worker phase create a Run-native Finding even though simple@v1 has no review phase; an open blocking Finding correctly prevents completion and causes a terminal awaiting_human stop instead, per the reducer's existing completion_blocked_by_open_blocking_findings mechanics -- the same fail-closed behavior exercised by SIG-ACT-WFC-FD08-FINDING-AUTHORITY-RECURRENCE above, in a different programme. direct@v1 and robust@v1 are unaffected by this delivery.
